novelty_basis: The asymptotics L(n) ~ phi^2 n are known (Cusenza et al.); an explicit O(log^2 n) error bound was not looked for in the literature.
proof_check: written proof with a Lean-checked arithmetic core - proofs/paper/C19.md Theorem 8: the split phase reaches lazy(n) after Psi(lazy(n)) moves, so L(n) >= Psi(lazy(n)) and D(n) <= B(n) - Psi(lazy(n)) (written; the argument is the Skeptic's, reviews/skeptic_C13_C19.md C9, written out and checked by the Director); the estimate B(n) - Psi(lazy(n)) <= 1 + (t+1)(t+6)/2 - the weight identity a_(k+1) = phi^2 F_(k+1) + psi^(k+2) - k - 3 and the bound for any two 0/1 strings of equal value with the second one vanishing above t - is Lean-checked (proofs/lean/Infinity/C19_DeficitBound.lean: weight_identity, deficit_bound, deficit_bound_int; standard axioms only); the bound holds on all 103,799 n of EXP-C19-05 (largest ratio 0.476)
statement: For every n, D(n) = B(n) - L(n) <= 1 + (t+1)(t+6)/2, where t is the top level of the lazy Fibonacci representation of n; consequently L(n) = phi^2 n - O(log^2 n). No optimality theorem is needed.
title: The deficit of the longest Zeckendorf game is O(log^2 n) - D(n) <= 1 + (t+1)(t+6)/2, so L(n) = phi^2 n - O(log^2 n)
